audit_status.source_base: Hebrew Numbers / Bemidbar vow and oath text tradition, draft aligned later
audit_status.review_note: First-pass draft reviewed for binding male vows, daughters in fathers' houses, married women's vows, widowed/divorced women's autonomy, husband/father nullification, silence as confirmation, and transferred liability. Strong anti-patriarchy, anti-coercion, and medical-safety safeguards required.

verses.restored: Moses spoke to heads of tribes of children of Israel, saying: This is the word that YHWH commanded.

familiar.text: And Moses spake unto the heads of the tribes concerning the children of Israel, saying, This is the thing which the LORD hath commanded.

modern.text: Then Moses said to the heads of the tribes of Israel, “This is what the LORD has commanded:

original.text: וַיְדַבֵּ֤ר מֹשֶׁה֙ אֶל רָאשֵׁ֣י הַמַּטּ֔וֹת לִבְנֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל לֵאמֹ֑ר זֶ֣ה הַדָּבָ֔ר אֲשֶׁ֖ר צִוָּ֥ה יְהוָֽה

verses.restored: When a man vows a vow to YHWH or swears an oath to bind a binding obligation upon his soul/life, he shall not profane/break his word; according to all going out from his mouth he shall do.

familiar.text: If a man vow a vow unto the LORD, or swear an oath to bind his soul with a bond; he shall not break his word, he shall do according to all that proceedeth out of his mouth.

modern.text: If a man makes a vow to the LORD or swears an oath to obligate himself by a pledge, he must not break his word; he must do everything he has promised.

original.text: אִישׁ֩ כִּֽי יִדֹּ֨ר נֶ֜דֶר לַֽיהוָ֗ה אֽוֹ הִשָּׁ֤בַע שְׁבֻעָה֙ לֶאְסֹ֤ר אִסָּר֙ עַל נַפְשׁ֔וֹ לֹ֥א יַחֵ֖ל דְּבָר֑וֹ כְּכָל הַיֹּצֵ֥א מִפִּ֖יו יַעֲשֶֽׂה

verses.restored: When a woman vows a vow to YHWH and binds an obligation in house of her father in her youth,

familiar.text: If a woman also vow a vow unto the LORD, and bind herself by a bond, being in her father’s house in her youth;

modern.text: And if a woman in her father’s house during her youth makes a vow to the LORD or obligates herself by a pledge,

original.text: וְאִשָּׁ֕ה כִּֽי תִדֹּ֥ר נֶ֖דֶר לַיהוָ֑ה וְאָסְרָ֥ה אִסָּ֛ר בְּבֵ֥ית אָבִ֖יהָ בִּנְעֻרֶֽיהָ

verses.restored: and her father hears her vow and her obligation with which she bound her soul/life, and her father is silent toward her, then all her vows shall stand, and every obligation with which she bound her soul/life shall stand.

familiar.text: And her father hear her vow, and her bond wherewith she hath bound her soul, and her father shall hold his peace at her: then all her vows shall stand, and every bond wherewith she hath bound her soul shall stand.

modern.text: and her father hears about her vow or pledge but says nothing to her, then all the vows or pledges by which she has bound herself shall stand.

original.text: וְשָׁמַ֨ע אָבִ֜יהָ אֶת נִדְרָ֗הּ וֶֽאֱסָרָהּ֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר אָֽסְרָ֣ה עַל נַפְשָׁ֔הּ וְהֶחֱרִ֥ישׁ לָ֖הּ אָבִ֑יהָ וְקָ֨מוּ֙ כָּל נְדָרֶ֔יהָ וְכָל אִסָּ֛ר אֲשֶׁר אָסְרָ֥ה עַל נַפְשָׁ֖הּ יָקֽוּם

verses.restored: But if her father restrains her on day he hears, none of her vows or obligations with which she bound her soul/life shall stand; and YHWH will forgive her, because her father restrained her.

familiar.text: But if her father disallow her in the day that he heareth; not any of her vows, or of her bonds wherewith she hath bound her soul, shall stand: and the LORD shall forgive her, because her father disallowed her.

modern.text: But if her father prohibits her on the day he hears about it, then none of the vows or pledges by which she has bound herself shall stand. The LORD will absolve her because her father has prohibited her.

original.text: וְשָׁמַ֥ע אִישָׁ֛הּ בְּי֥וֹם שָׁמְע֖וֹ וְהֶחֱרִ֣ישׁ לָ֑הּ וְקָ֣מוּ נְדָרֶ֗יהָ וֶֽאֱסָרֶ֛הָ אֲשֶׁר אָסְרָ֥ה עַל נַפְשָׁ֖הּ יָקֻֽמוּ

modern.text: But if her husband prohibits her when he hears of it, he nullifies the vow that binds her or the rash promise she has made, and the LORD will absolve her.

modern.text: Every vow a widow or divorced woman pledges to fulfill is binding on her.

modern.text: But if her husband nullifies them on the day he hears of them, then nothing that came from her lips, whether her vows or pledges, shall stand. Her husband has nullified them, and the LORD will absolve her.

translation_notes: The chapter treats spoken vows as serious obligations and distinguishes deliberate commitment from rash utterance.

Its gender structure is explicitly patriarchal: fathers and husbands can nullify certain women's vows, while men's vows receive no equivalent female review. This asymmetry must be preserved for critique rather than harmonized away.
Widowed and divorced women are treated as responsible for their own vows, demonstrating that the control mechanism is household status rather than an alleged incapacity of women.
Silence on the day of hearing confirms the vow; delayed nullification transfers liability to the husband.
Vows to humble/afflict the self must not be used to require self-harm, medically unsafe fasting, financial ruin, or coercive religious performance.
Verse numbering differs between some Hebrew and English traditions because the opening statement may be attached to the preceding chapter.
safety_note: Do not use Numbers 30 to control women's speech, finances, bodies, relationships, religious commitments, or medical decisions. Do not coerce vows or unsafe ascetic practices. The source preserves an ancient patriarchal household law; modern ethical reception must center equal agency, informed consent, and freedom from coercion.
